issues.description: Field 'animals' in class Farm: the problem statement explicitly instructs that the Farm should use a List and initialize an ArrayList in the no-argument constructor, and the template contains a TODO to implement Farm accordingly. The solution implementation, however, declares the collection as a Set and initializes it with a HashSet (private Set<Animal> animals; this.animals = new HashSet<>()). This is an attribute type mismatch across artifacts and can confuse students about the intended collection semantics (ordering and duplicate handling) and lead to tests or example code that expect List-specific behavior failing or producing different results.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: update the solution to use List<Animal> and initialize an ArrayList in the no-argument constructor (change declaration to 'private List<Animal> animals;' and constructor to 'this.animals = new ArrayList<>();', and adjust getter/setter types to List<Animal>). Alternative: if using a Set is intentional, update the problem statement and template to specify Set/HashSet and explain the change in semantics. Prefer the first option to match the explicit instruction in the problem statement.
